According to Steamboat Springs resident Dora Stockton, the secret to a long, happy life is based on three things: peace, friendliness and truthfulness. She would know; she turned 100 on April 4. A Michigan native, Stockton grew up in Pontiac. She raised her two boys in Waterford, Michigan, and worked as a secretary and bookkeeper for more than 40 years. In August 2005, she moved to Steamboat to live with her son, Bill, and daughter-in-law, Lucelia. An avid reader, Stockton keeps up-to-date on current affairs and enjoys dinner time conversations with family and friends. Reflecting on the greatest changes in her lifetime, she said, “Going from the horse and buggy era, to automobiles and now, travel into space.” Her gentle smile never falters as she discusses how she spends her days. “Writing letters to friends, working on a crossword puzzle, watching baseball or family movies,” Stockton said.

June 4, 2017 - Nablus, Palestine - Samaritans participate in a traditional ceremony celebrating the giving of the Torah on ''Shavuot festival'', atop Mount Gerizim near the West Bank city of Nablus. Shavuot Festival, known as the Feast of Weeks and as Pentecost in ancient Greek, is a Jewish holiday that occurs on the sixth day of the Hebrew month of Sivan. The Samaritan is a religious group that split from Judaism by the second century B.C.E. The Samaritans retained the Torah, the Five Books of Moses, as their Scripture. The Samaritan Bible refers to Mt. Gerizim, not Jerusalem, as the center of worship. (Credit Image: © Yunjie Liao/Pacific Press via ZUMA Wire)
